invariants.text: Register geometry shifts with width: MSI 64-bit permission moves the data word; MSI-X pointers split into selector plus aligned offset; allocation base and limit share one address mask.
Multi-field words are decoded by masking and shifting rather than direct equality, including extended header identifier, version and next pointer plus budget values.
Virtual-function resizable BAR selectors reuse the physical-function capability and control offsets and masks rather than independent encodings.
Discovery response protocol selector equals the discovery response type selector rather than an independent encoding.

state_machines.text: Migration state is a two-bit value for unavailable, migrate-in, migrate-out and available. Table pointer packs a BAR selector in low bits with remaining high bits forming an aligned offset.
Containment status latches triggered, interrupt and busy conditions.

structs.text: MSI message control at offset 2 carries enable, multi-message capable and enabled fields, 64-bit permission and masking capability. Lower address is at 4 with upper at 8 when 64-bit; data moves from 8 to 12.

MSI-X control at offset 2 encodes table size plus mask-all and enable. Table at 4 and pending array at 8 each combine BAR selector with aligned offset. Each 16-byte entry holds addresses, data and vector control with a mask bit.

Advanced Features advertises reset capability with control to initiate it. Enhanced Allocation header gives count and first offset; each entry encodes BAR indicator, properties, enable, base and limit.

PCI Express capability at offset 2 carries version, device or port type including endpoint, root port and switch ports, slot present and interrupt number. Device capabilities at 4 report payload, tags, latencies, indicators, power and reset.

Device control at 8 enables error reporting and ordering plus payload and read-request size selection and reset. Status at 0xA latches error conditions and transactions pending. Version-1 root endpoints without link are 12 bytes.
Link capabilities at 0xC report max speed and width with ASPM support. Control at 0x10 governs ASPM, retrain and disable. Status at 0x12 reports current speed and width plus training and active.

Slot capabilities at 0x14 describe button, power control, indicators, surprise and hot-plug plus slot number. Slot control at 0x18 enables hot-plug events. Slot status and root registers near 0x1A-0x20 carry latches, error and PME enables and requester.

Second-generation device registers near 0x24-0x2A advertise timeout, routing, atomic, latency and prefix features with matching enables. Link registers near 0x2C-0x32 carry supported and target speed vectors plus flit status and slot presence-disable.

Extended header splits into 16-bit identifier, 4-bit version and aligned next pointer. Identifiers form a fixed registry from error reporting through 64 GT/s physical layer covering virtualization, power, containment, channels and encryption.
Uncorrectable status and severity at 0x04-0x0C separate link, packet and request faults. Correctable status and mask at 0x10-0x14 plus header log and root command and status complete reporting.

Virtual-channel port and per-resource registers manage arbitration tables, channel enables and negotiation with base size and stride. Power budgeting packs base, scale, state and rail. Event-collector bitmap and vendor header identify associations.

Alternate routing advertises group capability with next-function and enable. Translation gives queue depth, page-aligned flag, enable and unit size. Page request adds counts, enable, reset and failure status. Address-space support adds width, execute and privilege.

Single-root virtualization carries capability and control, initial, total and active counts, offset, stride, device identifier, page size and address slots. Control governs virtual enable with routing and migration options.

Access control pairs capability with control and egress vector for source, redirect and forwarding protections. Latency reporting uses snoop and no-snoop halfwords with value and scale. Resizable BAR pairs sizes with index, count and size selector.

Downstream containment uses capability, control, status and source identifier. Capability advertises software trigger; enables cover fatal and nonfatal; status latches triggered, reason, interrupt and busy.

L1 substates use capability plus two control words mirroring PCI and ASPM L1.1 and L1.2 enables with timing fields. Object exchange gives capability, control with go, status with busy, and read and write ports. Time support advertises roles with enable.
